title: Speciation; Biodiversity and its measurement
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV07a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV07a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV05a#t4 term and clue written for the game; EV07a#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV05a#N.2, EV07a#N.6b, EV05a#N.10a, EV07a#N.9b, EV05a#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Genetic diversity
items.clue: The variety of alleles within one species

items.label: Species richness
items.clue: The number of different kinds of organism present

items.label: Hybrid sterility
items.clue: Crossbred offspring live but cannot breed, as with the mule

items.label: Ecosystem diversity
items.clue: The range of habitats present, e.g. sand dune, woodland, meadow, stream

questions.stem: According to the biological species concept, what is a species?

options.text: A group of organisms that can mate and produce offspring of any kind
A group of organisms that can breed together and produce fertile offspring
A group of organisms that resemble one another in every visible trait
A group of organisms that live in the same area and interbreed with one another

questions.explanation: Fertility of the offspring is the decisive condition in the biological species concept.

questions.stem: Illustrative data. A rock pool holds limpets 8, barnacles 6, periwinkles 4 and sea anemones 2. Using D = 1 − Σ(n/N)², what is Simpson's Index of Diversity?

Two closely related bird species live in the same forest. The males of each species sing a different song, and females respond only to the song of their own species. What is the significance of this for the two species?

options.text: It is not a barrier to hybridisation, because only physical differences can stop two species breeding.
It lets the two species coexist by preventing them from competing with each other for food.
It shows that they are really one species, because they are so alike and live in the same forest.
It prevents hybridisation, so that alleles do not pass between the two gene pools.

questions.stem: Ecologists want to compare the species diversity of the plant communities in two meadows by calculating Simpson's Diversity Index for each. Which procedure is most appropriate?

options.text: List the different plant species found in each meadow, without counting the individuals of each.
Count the total number of plants in each meadow, without recording which species each belongs to.
Count the individuals of each species in several randomly placed quadrats of equal size in each meadow.
Count the individuals of each species in one quadrat placed in the middle of each meadow.

questions.stem: A population of lizards was split when rising sea level cut off an island from the mainland. Many generations later, island and mainland lizards can no longer produce fertile offspring together. Which statement about this speciation is correct?

options.text: Separation was enough by itself, and the two populations were different species as soon as they were cut off.
The populations only became different species once the lizards began to look different from one another.
Separation stopped gene flow, so selection on each side could change the two gene pools independently.
Lizards on the island developed the features they needed and then passed them on to their young.
